question: Create contour lines from Angola's population data in relation to power stations
finalAnswer:
Done — the contour layer and Angola power-station overlay are on the map.

Population uses the supplied WorldPop 2020 annual UN-adjusted raster in people per cell, not density. All five requested contour levels are present. Missing coverage remains where 947,409 source cells are masked, so contours stop at those gaps and at the raster edge.

Power uses the supplied USGS 2021 frozen compilation. I retained 80 Angola rows with benchmark_row_id; 78 draw as points because 2 source rows have no geometry.

Visually, several stations sit near higher-population contour clusters, especially in western and central Angola, while other contour clusters are away from mapped stations. This is a visual comparison only.

### Limitations

- This is a visual spatial comparison only. It does not establish causation or use buffers.
- The population raster is people per cell, not population density.
- Masked or nonfinite raster cells remain unknown and produce contour gaps.
- The power overlay uses the supplied USGS 2021 frozen compilation; 2 retained Angola rows have no source geometry, so only 78 points can draw on the map.
- The population source is WorldPop 2020 annual UN-adjusted population aggregated to 1 km cells, in people per cell, not population density.
- Band 1 has 947,409 masked or otherwise unknown source cells; contours stop at those gaps and at the outer edge.
- This is a visual spatial comparison only; it does not imply causation or use buffers.
- The overlay uses the supplied USGS 2021 frozen compilation, not a current inventory.
- Two retained Angola rows in the supplied power-station source have null geometry, so 78 points draw on the map although 80 Angola rows are retained in the overlay artifact.
